# shopping-cart

An in-memory `ShoppingCart` class. It started as a buggy example with five known defects; this repo fixes them and adds regression tests for each one.

## Usage

```js
const ShoppingCart = require('./src/cart');
const { ItemNotFoundError } = require('./src/errors');

const cart = new ShoppingCart();
cart.addItem('shirt', 20, 2);
cart.addItem('socks', 5, 1);
cart.addItem('shirt', 20, 1);   // same name: quantity becomes 3

cart.applyDiscount(10);         // 10% off
cart.getTotal();                // 58.5
cart.getItemCount();            // 2 (distinct lines)

cart.removeItem('socks');
cart.removeItem('socks');       // throws ItemNotFoundError

cart.addItem('hat', -5, 1);     // throws RangeError
cart.applyDiscount(150);        // throws RangeError
```

## Commands

Requires Node 22 or later. The tests use the built-in `node:test` runner, so `npm test` works without installing anything.

```sh
npm test          # all tests in tests/
npm install       # only needed for linting
npm run lint      # ESLint
```

## The five bugs

| # | Original behaviour | Fix (`src/cart.js`) | Regression tests (`tests/cart.test.js`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `addItem` stored negative prices and quantities. A negative quantity on an existing line shrank it. | Lines 34-35 validate price (finite, ≥ 0) and quantity (whole number, ≥ 1). Line 40 checks the merged quantity. | `bug 1: addItem rejects a negative price…`, `…negative quantity…`, `…cannot shrink an existing line` |
| 2 | `filter(i => i.name = name)` assigned instead of comparing. Every item was renamed to the removed name and none were removed. A missing name went unreported. | Line 55 keeps items with `i.name !== name`. Line 57 throws `ItemNotFoundError` when nothing matched. | `bug 2: removeItem keeps the other items…`, `bug 2: removeItem throws ItemNotFoundError…` |
| 3 | The loop ran `i <= length`, read `items[length]` (undefined) and threw a `TypeError` on every call, even on an empty cart. | Line 69 uses `for...of`, which cannot overrun. | `bug 3: getTotal stops at the last item…`, `bug 3: getTotal of an empty cart is 0…` |
| 4 | `total + total * discount / 100` added the discount. | Line 72 subtracts it. | `bug 4: getTotal subtracts the discount…` |
| 5 | `applyDiscount` accepted any value, including 150, -5 and `NaN`. | Line 81 requires a finite number from 0 to 100. | `bug 5: applyDiscount rejects a percentage above 100`, `…negative percentage` |

The comment on bug 2 suggested replacing `=` with `===`. That change alone is still wrong: the filter would then keep only the item being removed. The operator has to be `!==`. The tests catch both the original bug and the `===` version.

## Design decisions

These cover behaviour the original code left unspecified.

- **Invalid input throws.** A wrong type (a string, `NaN`, `Infinity`, `null`, a boxed `Number`) throws `TypeError`. A number outside the allowed range throws `RangeError`. Messages name the argument and the value received, e.g. `price must be 0 or greater, received -3`. Numeric strings are not coerced.
- **A rejected call changes nothing.** Every argument is checked before any state changes, so after a throw the items and discount are exactly as they were. `tests/cart.edge-cases.test.js` checks this for each kind of rejected call.
- **Removing a missing item throws `ItemNotFoundError`** and does not return `false`. A missing name usually means the caller has a stale or mistyped name, and a silent no-op would hide that. The error has an `itemName` property.
- **A price of 0 is allowed**, for free items. Negative prices are not.
- **Quantity must be a whole number from 1 to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`.** Zero and fractions are rejected. Past `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, addition loses precision, so a merge that would go over the limit is rejected as well.
- **Adding an existing name keeps the first price.** The original code did this. Changing it would change behaviour outside the five bugs, so it stays and is covered by a test.
- **Names are matched exactly.** Case and surrounding whitespace count, so `'Apple'` and `' apple '` are separate lines. A name must contain at least one non-whitespace character.
- **`removeItem` removes the whole line**, whatever its quantity.
- **A new discount replaces the old one.** Discounts do not stack.
- **`getItemCount` counts distinct lines, not units.** This is the original behaviour and was not one of the listed bugs.
- **Totals are not rounded.** With fractional prices, `getTotal` can return values like `0.30000000000000004`. How to round depends on the currency (JPY has no minor unit, KWD has three), so the cart leaves that to the caller. Prices given as integer minor units (cents) give exact totals.
- **Each cart has its own state.** Nothing is shared between instances, and the tests check that two carts don't affect each other.

### Not included

- **Configurable limits.** The task fixes the discount range at 0-100, and no other limit came up, so there are no constructor options.
- **Alternative algorithms.** The cart has no algorithm with real alternatives. The total is a single sum.
- **Concurrency tests.** Every method is synchronous and each cart has its own state, so there is no race to test. Instance isolation is tested instead.

## Layout

```
src/cart.js         ShoppingCart
src/validation.js   argument checks shared by the cart methods
src/errors.js       ItemNotFoundError
tests/cart.test.js              per-method tests and one regression block per bug
tests/cart.edge-cases.test.js   isolation, unicode and long names, large values, bulk adds, rejected-call atomicity, full workflow
tests/validation.test.js        unit tests for each validator
tests/helpers.js                float comparison and state snapshot helpers
```

## How the regression tests were checked

- Commit `1d2a0ef` holds the original buggy file. Run against it, all ten `bug N:` tests fail (61 of the 68 tests in `tests/cart.test.js` fail).
- Each bug was then put back into the fixed code on its own, in a scratch copy, and `node --test --test-name-pattern="^bug N:"` was run. Every one of these mutants failed at least one test for its own bug, and so did the `===` variant of bug 2.
- The `no-return-assign` rule in `eslint.config.js` also reports bug 2 in the original file, so the linter would have caught it without any tests.

# shopping-cart

An in-memory `ShoppingCart` class. It started as a buggy example with five known defects; this repo fixes them and adds regression tests for each one.

## Usage

```js
const ShoppingCart = require('./src/cart');
const { ItemNotFoundError } = require('./src/errors');

const cart = new ShoppingCart();
cart.addItem('shirt', 20, 2);
cart.addItem('socks', 5, 1);
cart.addItem('shirt', 20, 1);   // same name: quantity becomes 3

cart.applyDiscount(10);         // 10% off
cart.getTotal();                // 58.5
cart.getItemCount();            // 2 (distinct lines)

cart.removeItem('socks');
cart.removeItem('socks');       // throws ItemNotFoundError

cart.addItem('hat', -5, 1);     // throws RangeError
cart.applyDiscount(150);        // throws RangeError
```

## Commands

Requires Node 22 or later. The tests use the built-in `node:test` runner, so `npm test` works without installing anything.

```sh
npm test          # all tests in tests/
npm install       # only needed for linting
npm run lint      # ESLint
```

## The five bugs

| # | Original behaviour | Fix (`src/cart.js`) | Regression tests (`tests/cart.test.js`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `addItem` stored negative prices and quantities. A negative quantity on an existing line shrank it. | Lines 34-35 validate price (finite, ≥ 0) and quantity (whole number, ≥ 1). Line 40 checks the merged quantity. | `bug 1: addItem rejects a negative price…`, `…negative quantity…`, `…cannot shrink an existing line` |
| 2 | `filter(i => i.name = name)` assigned instead of comparing. Every item was renamed to the removed name and none were removed. A missing name went unreported. | Line 55 keeps items with `i.name !== name`. Line 57 throws `ItemNotFoundError` when nothing matched. | `bug 2: removeItem keeps the other items…`, `bug 2: removeItem throws ItemNotFoundError…` |
| 3 | The loop ran `i <= length`, read `items[length]` (undefined) and threw a `TypeError` on every call, even on an empty cart. | Line 69 uses `for...of`, which cannot overrun. | `bug 3: getTotal stops at the last item…`, `bug 3: getTotal of an empty cart is 0…` |
| 4 | `total + total * discount / 100` added the discount. | Line 72 subtracts it. | `bug 4: getTotal subtracts the discount…` |
| 5 | `applyDiscount` accepted any value, including 150, -5 and `NaN`. | Line 81 requires a finite number from 0 to 100. | `bug 5: applyDiscount rejects a percentage above 100`, `…negative percentage` |

The comment on bug 2 suggested replacing `=` with `===`. That change alone is still wrong: the filter would then keep only the item being removed. The operator has to be `!==`. The tests catch both the original bug and the `===` version.

## Design decisions

These cover behaviour the original code left unspecified.

- **Invalid input throws.** A wrong type (a string, `NaN`, `Infinity`, `null`, a boxed `Number`) throws `TypeError`. A number outside the allowed range throws `RangeError`. Messages name the argument and the value received, e.g. `price must be 0 or greater, received -3`. Numeric strings are not coerced.
- **A rejected call changes nothing.** Every argument is checked before any state changes, so after a throw the items and discount are exactly as they were. `tests/cart.edge-cases.test.js` checks this for each kind of rejected call.
- **Removing a missing item throws `ItemNotFoundError`** and does not return `false`. A missing name usually means the caller has a stale or mistyped name, and a silent no-op would hide that. The error has an `itemName` property.
- **A price of 0 is allowed**, for free items. Negative prices are not.
- **Quantity must be a whole number from 1 to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`.** Zero and fractions are rejected. Past `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, addition loses precision, so a merge that would go over the limit is rejected as well.
- **Adding an existing name keeps the first price.** The original code did this. Changing it would change behaviour outside the five bugs, so it stays and is covered by a test.
- **Names are matched exactly.** Case and surrounding whitespace count, so `'Apple'` and `' apple '` are separate lines. A name must contain at least one non-whitespace character.
- **`removeItem` removes the whole line**, whatever its quantity.
- **A new discount replaces the old one.** Discounts do not stack.
- **`getItemCount` counts distinct lines, not units.** This is the original behaviour and was not one of the listed bugs.
- **Totals are not rounded.** With fractional prices, `getTotal` can return values like `0.30000000000000004`. How to round depends on the currency (JPY has no minor unit, KWD has three), so the cart leaves that to the caller. Prices given as integer minor units (cents) give exact totals.
- **Each cart has its own state.** Nothing is shared between instances, and the tests check that two carts don't affect each other.

### Not included

- **Configurable limits.** The task fixes the discount range at 0-100, and no other limit came up, so there are no constructor options.
- **Alternative algorithms.** The cart has no algorithm with real alternatives. The total is a single sum.
- **Concurrency tests.** Every method is synchronous and each cart has its own state, so there is no race to test. Instance isolation is tested instead.

## Layout

```
src/cart.js         ShoppingCart
src/validation.js   argument checks shared by the cart methods
src/errors.js       ItemNotFoundError
tests/cart.test.js              per-method tests and one regression block per bug
tests/cart.edge-cases.test.js   isolation, unicode and long names, large values, bulk adds, rejected-call atomicity, full workflow
tests/validation.test.js        unit tests for each validator
tests/helpers.js                float comparison and state snapshot helpers
```

I fixed all five bugs in `src/cart.js`. The test suite passes (127 of 127) and ESLint reports no problems. Each bug has regression tests, and I confirmed they fail on the original code.

**The bugs and fixes**

| # | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `addItem` accepted negative prices and quantities | Price must be a finite number, 0 or more. Quantity must be a whole number, 1 or more. A merge that would make the quantity too large is also rejected. (`src/cart.js:34-40`) |
| 2 | `removeItem` used `=`, which renamed every item and removed nothing | Now uses `!==`, and removing a name that isn't in the cart throws `ItemNotFoundError` (`src/cart.js:55-57`) |
| 3 | `getTotal` looped with `<=`, so it threw on every call, even for an empty cart | Uses `for...of` (`src/cart.js:69`) |
| 4 | The discount was added to the total | It's now subtracted (`src/cart.js:72`) |
| 5 | `applyDiscount` accepted any value | Only finite numbers from 0 to 100 are accepted (`src/cart.js:81`) |

The comment on bug 2 suggests changing `=` to `===`. That fix is also wrong, because the filter would then keep only the item being removed. The tests catch that version too.

**How I checked the tests**
- **Against the original code:** I committed the original file first (`1d2a0ef`) and wrote the tests before fixing anything. All ten tests labelled `bug N:` failed on it.
- **One bug at a time:** in a temporary copy, I put each bug back into the fixed code on its own. Each time, at least one of that bug's own tests failed.
- **Lint:** I added ESLint with the `no-return-assign` rule, which flags bug 2 in the original file.

**Files**
- **Code:** `src/cart.js`, plus `src/validation.js` for input checks and `src/errors.js` for `ItemNotFoundError`.
- **Tests:** `tests/cart.test.js` has the tests for each method plus the bug tests. There are also edge-case tests and unit tests for the input checks.
- **Setup and docs:** `package.json` (`npm test` uses Node's built-in test runner, so it needs no install), `eslint.config.js` and `README.md`.

**Choices you may want to change** (explained in the README)
- Removing an item that isn't in the cart throws an error instead of returning `false`.
- Bad input throws `TypeError` for the wrong type or `RangeError` for an out-of-range value. A call that throws leaves the cart unchanged.
- A price of 0 is allowed. Quantities must be whole numbers.
- Adding a name that's already in the cart keeps the first price, as the original code did.
- Totals aren't rounded, so `0.1 + 0.2` gives `0.30000000000000004`.

**Git and process**
- The work is in six commits on the branch `fix/cart-bugs`. There's no remote, so nothing was pushed, and I left `CLAUDE.md` untracked.
- A hook in this environment required conventional commit messages and a Dex co-author line, so I used those instead of the Claude attribution line.
